reviews.text:
First time here at Luna, of course, I had to ask If Giada was in the house.  Sad to say, she was not present.  I wanted her to prepare my dinner, oh well, maybe next time.  Everything was outstanding, there was 8 of us celebrating our beautiful friend 's birthday (Sara). I started with a spicy Negroni cocktail which was decadent.  We shared, bread, Misso Frito, and Lobster Cream Puff as starters. I followed with an Arugula salad and my entree was the Lemon Spaghetti Pasta. Wowie, this dish was amazing!  The flavors were exquisite! We took our time eating, conversing, and sharing our memories while sampling each other's plates. For dessert, we shared something like chocolate cream puffs with caramel sauce which would have been a sin not to eat at least one!  And our birthday girl  (Sara) ended her meal with a slice of Giada's birthday cake, our Happy Birthday Song, her special wish, and a few tears to end our fabulous celebration.
Special shout out to wonderful waiter!  He was excellent!
reviews.author: Antonio Sanchez

reviews.text:
Luna by Giada is the highest level of quality In food, service, and atmosphere. A large group of us celebrated my sister‘s 50th birthday. We were seated right on time and started with drinks and appetizers. Highly recommend the meatballs and calamari. The citrus Caesar salad was also a big hit.

I split the porterhouse steak with my son-in-law. The steak was the best I’ve ever had. It was grass fed and locally sourced from upstate in Arizona. The seafood that we had is flown in each day and is fresh. The ravioli and signature lemon pasta were phenomenal.

The wine and drink selection was great and perfectly made. I’ve never had a better old-fashioned than I had at Luna. Our server was incredibly knowledgeable and gave great dinner and wine recommendations.

Dessert should not be missed at Luna. My sister was treated with a slice of cannoli cake for her birthday, which we all enjoyed. I strongly recommend the strawberry soufflé as it was heavenly.

The only slight disappointment was that we were not seated in the area where you can watch the open kitchen. That was probably because our party was such a large size. The next time I visit I definitely want to sit in the area where you can watch the chef’s cook.

The other thing that was a bit annoying was that you’re charged a 3 1/2% administrative fee on your bill. It says it in the menu so you’re not surprised when it’s added.
reviews.author: Susann Braverman

reviews.text:
I have never in my life walked up to the hostess stand and made a reservation for the next night, but I did tonight.

My wife and I shared everything to maximize what we tried, starting with the focaccia and lobster arancini. Both were incredible! Followed by the signature pasta and branzino, also perfect! Beyond perfect! We chased all of that with espresso, raspberry sorbet, and soufflé. Everything was perfectly executed!

Beyond that the staff was friendly, enthusiastic, and all around top notch. We’re vacationing in Scottsdale and hit up several well reviewed restaurants…this one is Michelin level.
reviews.author: Stephen Massi

reviews.text: Never underestimate the power of superior service. Hostess was so welcoming, and our waitress, Melanie, took things to the highest level.
reviews.author: Scott Hutchinson

reviews.text: This was not our first visit to Luna, but it will always be our most memorable!  The owner blessed us with a table side visit! She was very gracious with her time, was genuinely present with us.  We e left feeling we made a new friend!  Of course she won't be there for every future visit, but that won't change the memories we made of this one!

reviews.text: Incredible experience. First time here visiting from Oregon for a bachelorette party. Brandi took care of us on the patio and she was the best server I have come across in a long time. Knowledge of the menu was very impressive, and she even gave us tips on where to enjoy the rest of the week in Scottsdale. We had a little bit of everything and everything that she recommended was a 10/10!!! Thank you Brandi for making our night so great and kicking off our vacation! Cheers! Highly recommend! Ask for BRANDI!!!

reviews.text: Malanie is an amazing waitress! We had the most amazing dinner with delicious food and she was so attentive to our needs. This is our fourth time coming here and always having her and it makes every experience so special! Will be coming back!

reviews.text: This was our third time at brunch and will be the last. Upon greeting we were offered champagne, which was nice, but the glass was dirty. “Oh sorry. It should have been polished.” How about starting with washing it. They then had plastic cups of champagne. So cheap. On Mother’s Day, not once did anyone ask me how things were, not my food, not can I get you more coffee. Nothing. The service was nonexistent. I never saw my server but once and then again when the bill was presented. For $150 a person, coffee should be included BTW. And if you’re going to charge for it, you should be offering refills! The food was poor compared to last two. There was less variety and the focus was on the seafood, carving station, and salmon. This all sounds great unless you are not a meat-eater. The items I enjoyed in the past were gone. The bagels were stale! They were awful. Just bad quality and small. The waffles were the kind you make for your kids at a limited service hotel and were presented in a cast iron closed dish so they were soggy as were pancakes. Last time someone was making fresh ones for you with a lovely berry sauce which was not offered. They had limited salads and it was served “family style” not plated as in the past, so it was a messy plate of arugula with slices on cheese covering the top. I really missed their tomato salad. Not a tomato in site anywhere on any station. Except there were a few whole tomatoes for decor on the buffet. If you’re serving lox and “bagels” it is a must to have tomatoes. The pastries were definitely not the same quality and they were wiped out. Two croissants and some dry looking banana bread (? Not really sure what it was.) definitely not made in-house and if it was, it was shameful. The pasta was cold and the smashed potatoes, carrots and Brussel  sprouts were so unappealing looking, also cold. Not sure why because they were in closed chaffing dishes. The dessert selection was also limited compared to past brunches. Overall, I was so disappointed. Increasing the price, decreasing the selection, downgrading the quality, adding an “admin fee” , charging for coffee, and the awful service were not worth what we spent. I was very much looking forward to a wonderful brunch but instead felt like an inconvenience to the staff and ripped off. Unhappy Mother’s Day to me.

reviews.text:
By far the WORST experience I’ve had at a fine dining restaurant
We visited Luna by Giada at Caesars Republic in Scottsdale last night for my aunt’s birthday with a party of eight. We had a reservation for 7:00 PM and were seated around 7:20 PM, which was fine since we were still waiting for the rest of our group.
From the moment we sat down, our server told us she would get our drinks and courses in, and then we essentially never saw her again. Each course took nearly an hour to arrive at our table. It was a constant struggle to find someone just to get drink refills, condiments for our pizza and other food, or anything else we needed. We repeatedly had to track down other staff because our server never came back to check on us — not once to see if the food was okay or if we needed anything.
The only person who checked on our table was the assistant manager or manager. He was kind enough to bring us some free desserts and did mention that the restaurant/kitchen was behind, so at least that much was communicated. However, for our assigned server to completely disappear and not even come back to the table to make sure we were taken care of in the meantime felt COWARDLY and UNFAIR.
It was uncomfortable to even bring anything up to her because she had avoided our table so much — I didn’t want to say anything that might make things worse for her if she was already having a bad night. She showed no remorse and didn’t seem to care at all about how the experience was going for us. But at the end of the day, it’s just unfair to our party of eight. The painfully slow pacing and complete lack of attention made the entire evening uncomfortable and stressful instead of celebratory. None of us could enjoy ourselves, and it really ruined what should have been a happy night for my aunt’s birthday.
Despite all of this, the bill still included the automatic 20% gratuity for our large party, and she was tipped out anyway. That felt very unfair after being essentially abandoned.
As someone who has worked in the service industry — previously at the Global Ambassador and currently in elevated dining — this was by far the worst experience I’ve had at a fine dining restaurant. This level of neglect is unacceptable, especially for a first-time visit to a restaurant associated with Giada De Laurentiis. The whole meal took four hours, and I didn’t get home until midnight. I had to work the next morning and was extremely grateful that a coworker switched shifts with me, or I wouldn’t have made it in.
I really wanted this to be a memorable, happy night, but the terrible service completely overshadowed everything. Unless Luna by Giada improves their staff training and ensures servers actually attend to their tables (especially larger parties), I will not be returning. Anyone considering dining here should know ahead of time how neglectful the service can be.
reviews.author: Kalea Duran

reviews.text:
We went there with a group of eight and had a reservation, but it still took about 30 minutes to be seated. Once we were finally seated, it took quite a while for our waitress to come over and take our drink order.

We were very hungry and asked to order some appetizers right away, but the waitress told us they prefer to submit appetizer orders together with the dinner order to make things less hectic for the kitchen staff—which was something I had never heard before.

Unfortunately, it got worse. Our food took about an hour and a half to arrive, and during that time, the waitress never came by to update us about the delay. Eventually, my friend spoke with the manager, and about 15 minutes later, our food finally came out.

Our reservation was at 7:00 PM, and we didn’t finish dinner until 10:45 PM, which was extremely frustrating. The manager did try to make things right by offering complimentary desserts for the table, which we appreciated, but overall the experience was disappointing.

This was our first time at what’s considered a high-end restaurant, and the first impression was honestly terrible. I ordered the special with filet, prawns, and scallops over mashed potatoes, but the mashed potatoes were very salty. The lemon pasta was also overly salty.

I consider myself a foodie, so this experience was especially disappointing. This is just my personal opinion—others may have a different experience, but unfortunately, I wouldn’t go back.
reviews.author: Sitharath Sam

reviews.text:
Beautiful restaurant and great food. Our group sat on the patio and it was lovely. Not overcrowded.

Where the experience really stood out was the service provided by the General Manager, Angelo. I accidentally left my credit card at the restaurant. Although we couldn’t find it immediately, Angelo contacted me at my hotel later in the evening once it had been found. It was already late in the evening and I had a 6 AM flight in the morning (I was staying by the Airport and didn’t have a car). He personally delivered my credit card to my hotel on his way home from working his shift. It was incredibly kind of him to do this as it avoided a lot of hassle on my end replacing the card.

Great service goes a long way, and in addition to the overall experience, I look forward to going back the next time I’m in town.

reviews.text: This evening I have to admit was pretty ne for the books. After a subpar dinner service at Luna our server PATRICIA actually charged us $218 for an $86 ticket. Zero explanation for what absolutely feels like a scam and untrustworthy business. Not apologies and no explanation, if we had not received alerts from our credit card, would they have processed this. The manager on duty, Michael corrected the charge after I challenged them but needless to say we will not be back. Luna despite the backing of a celebrity chef misses the mark. It’s a hotel restaurant with random staff that pretends to be an Italian restaurant. Fails to deliver authentic cuisine and the fact that I was almost robbed seals the deal as an avoid at all cost outing.

reviews.author: jonathan weeks

reviews.text:
I recently visited Luna for a corporate dinner event, and it was my first time dining at the restaurant. From the moment we arrived, the ambiance stood out, the space is absolutely beautiful and sets the tone for a memorable experience. The food was exceptional, easily deserving five stars across the board. In particular, the scallop risotto and lemon spaghetti were highlights for me; both dishes were outstanding in flavor and execution.

What truly elevated the evening, however, was the service. The two young ladies who took care of our group exceeded all expectations. Our entire party consistently commented on their attention to detail, professionalism, and the ease with which they managed the evening. Brandi, who specifically handled my table, was phenomenal, knowledgeable, attentive, and clearly passionate about her work. Her energy and care made a lasting impression and truly enhanced our experience.

There was one aspect of the evening that fell short of an otherwise five-star visit. During our time in the dining room, I noticed a lack of engagement from the only manager I observed, who appeared to be the general manager. Despite being present on the floor, there was no greeting or acknowledgment upon arrival, even with direct proximity and eye contact. In my experience, that initial interaction plays an important role in setting the tone for hospitality, and its absence made the welcome feel less warm than expected.

That said, the outstanding service we received from Brandi and her colleague more than made up for this, and they ultimately turned the evening into a fantastic experience. I did share this feedback during our visit, as I believe constructive input is valuable for continued growth.

I look forward to returning and hope that next time the overall experience, from arrival to departure, reflects the same high level of hospitality demonstrated by the service team.
reviews.author: TGrantSales

reviews.text:
Went for an early dinner and had a really great experience overall. Service was attentive, friendly, and made the whole night feel relaxed without being overbearing. The cocktails were a standout—highly recommend the Italian Paloma. As a bit of a cocktail connoisseur, it was the kind of drink that’s perfectly balanced and elevated, and honestly not something I’d even try to replicate at home—it’s worth going out for.

The menu leans toward small plates and shareables, which we loved for trying a variety of things. The GF signature pasta was good, but the sauce didn’t quite live up to expectations—I was hoping for a little more depth of flavor. That said, the Brussels sprouts were absolutely perfect! Crispy, flavorful, and one of the best dishes we had. The caprese salad was also a hit, super fresh and so good we were basically licking the plate by the end.

Overall, a great spot with a fun atmosphere, standout drinks, and a few dishes that really shine. Would definitely come back.
reviews.author: Amelia Elizabeth

reviews.text:
My husband and I stayed at Caesars Republic last week and what a great surprise to learn that Luna was in the hotel. We had dinner there and dessert and coffee on our last night.  For dinner my husband had the chicken with Marsala wine and it was outstanding.    I had the pistachio pesto with sausage and broccoli rabe.  Way too much pesto and I never saw the sausage.
Dessert - the latte was perfect but the soufflé not so good.  The ingredients were separated and I tasted egg and there was liquid in the bottom of the mug it was served in.  I bake. This is not the way soufflé should be served.
I love Giada so will definitely try again when in Scottsdale but it could use some improvement in the kitchen.
reviews.author: Foodie Galore

reviews.text:
It pains me to write this because we were so excited about our evening out at Luna. Our party of four left feeling very disappointed about the entire experience. To begin the evening, three of us ordered martinis, one ordered a glass of wine off of the wine list, about which our server raved. The martinis were terrific and were brought to the table quickly, but we sat waiting for the glass of wine for at least 20 minutes, and we were ultimately told that they could not locate the particular wine we had ordered. So another wine was chosen for the glass of wine. When it came time to order and receive a bottle of wine for the table, two more times they ultimately discovered that didn’t have what we had selected. The manager did end up covering the cost of the bottle we finally ended up with (choice number 3) but this all occurred after the server made a point of telling us about their incredible wine selection. It was just odd. We ordered the bacon-wrapped dates and a margarita pizza for appetizers, and they were good. For entrees, two of us ordered the signature lemon spaghetti; one ordered lobster; one ordered the pasta à la vodka with scallops. The lemon spaghetti was beautiful, and it was “good” but definitely not great or amazing. The pasta à la vodka was sub par; it was just “ok”, meh. The scallops were perfectly seared, but not very flavorful. The lobster was good, but very small for $120.00 à la carte. Very underwhelming overall.
The restaurant is beautiful; the staff was kind; and we did love that the noise level was such that we could easily carry on a conversation. But the food was simply “ok” - nothing we could want to eat again.

reviews.text: Shoutout to Angelo, the Manager and Megan our server, for a delicious meal and outstanding service.

reviews.text:
Beautiful Italian restaurant with a great variety of fresh dishes. The restaurant itself was stunning. Every staff member was extremely knowledgeable about the menu and was very attentive.

Our table got a variety of the dishes including:
-focaccia bread - fresh and delicious
-meatballs - very good
-arugula salad (modified to be vegetarian) - best arugula salad I’ve ever had
-vegetable rigatoni - rich and delicious
-sausage pizza - solid wood fire pizza
-lemon spaghetti - very rich and creamy

Overall, we really liked our experience here. We did feel the meal was a little slow; we were starving and hoped the food would have come out quicker.

reviews.text: This being a consensus of opinion of us four. The restaurant was bustling, We didn't imagine it to be such a massive operation. Huge place. The decor was super impressive.The wait staff for the most part was good. Our server detailed all the answers to all of our questions. In some cases; a little  too much response from the server (if there is such a thing?). Our main server was very friendly; while the other server was not so much so. She was acceptable. We ordered a myriad of items.The two pizzas we outstanding. Not good; they were great!  Almost perfect.The salads were fine. The CRAB ARANCINI lacked a good amount of actual crab; but with good quality. While earlier reviews show their were five pieces; the restaurant has cut back to four. Two people in our group ordered salmon. While nicely prepared and tasted very good, For what it was; the portion size was not ample. For $52; our suggestion to to the restaurant is to increase the piece size at least a few ounces of the salmon. It was too modest. The MEZZI RIGATONI had nice flavor and seemed to be a solid choice. The SIGNATURE LEMON SPAGHETTI was way too rich for our tastes. Other diners; obviously may disagree. It was our least favorite of the meal. We ordered two orders of al-carte two pieces of shrimp; which as top notch and couldn't be better. On one of our bills it was priced at $20. The other bill showed the two shrimp to be $32. We caught that; and the bill was adjusted. The server said "The price of shrimp went up thanks to their recent cost of food; from their supplier."  We thought that was a pretty hefty increase from $20-$32 for just two shrimp. We ordered the cookie plate for dessert. The lemon cookie was excellent.The chocolate chip with sea salt was just fair. The presentation of everything was top notch. The overall 4 out 5 stars. The value of what we ordered ok; for what the bill was.It was not so great. Just because it's a high quality restaurant doesn't mean they need to be stingy on certain portions that they serve. Very pricey. Great ambience to the eye (Restaurant decor and food presentaion). A tad loud...but we could still chat (no problem) at the table. Would we go back?  Probably. We might do things alittle different on our next visit? We liked it. We didn't "love" the whole experience.For sure...more good; than not so good. All of us at our table are food critics. 4 out 5 stars.

reviews.text: We were in town (Phoenix) for Mardi Gras week that also coincided with Valentine's Day, and our reservation was for a somewhat later-than-usual dinner time (20:15) on Valentine's Day.  Valet parking was extremely chaotic/disorganized, and once inside we still had to wait ~35 minutes to be seated (beyond our on-time arrival).  The Host was kind enough to provide a glass of sparkling wine for us while we waited, which was a nice touch.  The surroundings were extremely swanky (VERY satisfied with the ambiance), but the menu was extremely uninspired - very basic, predictable fare.  Service was rather poor (our server was very inattentive), and the food was decent but again, very basic and a bit insipid actually.  The cocktail menu was equally uninspired, and despite the ho-hum options (which you'd think ANY bartender on the planet could easily make), our cocktails were rather poor quality; in fact, neither my wife nor I finished either of our cocktails, switching swiftly to wine instead.  Had this been any other restaurant, I would have given it at least 3-stars, but my expectations for Luna FAR exceeded what was ultimately delivered, and so I feel I must rate our experience a bit more harshly.  Very disappointed...
reviews.author: Scott Milroy

reviews.text:
My dining experience at Luna by Giada completely exceeded my expectations.

I’m someone who is quite particular about food and service, yet everything here felt thoughtful, polished, and genuinely welcoming. From the two lovely hostesses at the front to every server and manager inside, the hospitality was warm and refined. They gracefully placed the napkin on my lap, checked in attentively without being intrusive, and even offered to help take photos when they noticed I enjoyed photographing my dishes — such a thoughtful touch.

I ordered the Signature Lemon Spaghetti (sautéed shrimp, mascarpone cheese, basil & crispy capers). It has a distinct personality — bright, creamy, and beautifully balanced. The shrimp were impressively large and fresh. The tableside fresh pepper service with the oversized grinder added a charming finishing touch. Toward the end it felt slightly rich for my lighter palate, but overall it was excellent.

The Crab Arancini were perfectly crisp outside and tender inside, with sweet crab flavor complemented by calabrian pomodoro sauce.

For wine, I had the Rosé of Falanghina DOCG (Fontanavecchia, Campania) — refreshing and clean, pairing beautifully with the lemon shrimp pasta.

For dessert, I trusted my server’s recommendation — his personal favorite. A delicate pastry filled with pistachio cream, lightly infused with what seemed like rum, served with caramel shards and condensed milk. Sweet with a slight bitterness from the caramel — a surprisingly delightful combination.

Before leaving, I told the hostess I would definitely return. She asked my name (Mara), and even called goodbye as I was walking away. That small gesture made the evening even more memorable.

This is truly a restaurant that makes you want to come back.

reviews.text: Luna absolutely meets expectations! We’ve had the occasion to dine at Luna a couple of times over the last several weeks. On both occasions, our fellow diners along with my wife and I experienced a wide sampling of the menu and were all thoroughly pleased. Last night, our waitress, Melanie, did an outstanding job of presenting the menu and explaining the various options. The entire staff made the dining experience a pleasure. Some of favorites… The lemon pizza is definitely worth a try, especially as an appetizer; The signature lemon spaghetti, of course is a must try at some point. But don’t ignore the two wash ranch half chicken, which is the best chicken marsala I have ever had.. Oh yes, we ordered a side of the crispy brussels sprouts as an appetizer as well, and they are dynamite. another favorite was the Nodi marini à la vodka. It’s also nice that you can order additional proteins such as shrimp, scallops, sausage, etc. to be added to any dish. Well, we were thoroughly pleased with everything and certainly excited that it lived up to Giada‘s reputation. Highly recommend!
reviews.author: Michael Walker

reviews.text:
Luna by Giada has a beautiful atmosphere and the service was excellent from start to finish. The staff was attentive, friendly, and knowledgeable, and their wine selection is genuinely impressive.

That said, the food didn’t match the price point. The Italian dishes felt very overpriced for the quality, and the seafood in particular was overcooked and disappointing. For what you pay, I expected better execution in the kitchen.

Overall, it’s a lovely place to sit, enjoy wine, and be well taken care of — but based on the food alone, I’m not sure the value is there.
reviews.author: Jody

reviews.text: Worst service I have ever had a restaurant! Out of 6 people no one finished their food!
reviews.author: monteca (Confers Jewelers)

reviews.text:
I originally went to Wolf and had a very poor experience with the bartender. I felt rushed while ordering, which made the experience uncomfortable, so I decided to leave and go downstairs to Luna instead.

While sitting at Luna, I was next to a woman who was friends with one of the hosts. I briefly explained my experience at Wolf to her. She shared it with her hostess friend, who then came over to me, apologized sincerely, and said she would get a manager to address the situation.

When the manager arrived  I believe her name was Deana or possibly Daniella??? her demeanor was extremely rude and unpleasant. She had a very stiff attitude, showed little interest in listening or resolving the issue, and did not offer any meaningful acknowledgment or solution. Her behavior was uncomfortable enough that it even made the guest sitting next to me feel awkward.

I appreciate the host’s professionalism and kindness, but the manager’s response completely missed the mark and left a negative impression on my experience.

I was interested in having my parents Anniversary party here at Caesars hotel. That will not be happening.

reviews.text:
Our dining experiences at Luna by Giada have been nothing short of exceptional.

During our first visit, we reserved the private dining room for a family gathering. Nearly everything went perfectly, and I want to specifically spotlight our server, Kendal, who was absolutely amazing. Attentive, warm, professional, and truly elevated the entire private-room experience. It was clear she cared deeply about service and detail.

What truly sets Luna by Giada apart, however, is their commitment to excellence. Striving for perfection, they graciously invited my wife and me back for another evening—and that second visit was a true 10/10 experience from start to finish.

Our server this evening, Charese, was phenomenal. She was on point the entire night—knowledgeable, polished, perfectly paced, and genuinely welcoming. Every recommendation, every interaction, every detail was handled flawlessly.

It was also a pleasure connecting with Paul and Ken, who came by our table to personally introduce themselves as part of the upper management team and ensure everything was going great. That level of leadership presence speaks volumes about the culture here. A special shoutout to Melissa who handles the events. She personally oversaw both reservations from the private event to this evening.

Luna by Giada prioritizes the guest experience, and you feel that from the very moment you arrive. The service, the food, the atmosphere, and the people all come together seamlessly.

Highly recommend. This is a restaurant that truly puts the consumer first—and it shows.
reviews.author: Simran Lamba

reviews.text: We were a party of 6 on Christmas and I’m trying to be nice here since the staff was working a holiday. However, with the prices this place charges I would expect WAY better service than the subpar we received. Our total bill was over $400 and it wasn’t worth it I can tell you this. Like many reviews, they push the $16 bread on you right away making it sound like it’s on the house and then you see the exorbitant price and it wasn’t enough for 6 people. They claim to have the man server and their assistant, again you would expect this for the pricing, but they were terrible. Had to ask for water multiple times, then never got it but once. The wine was good but again very slow to see if you wanted more. The sculpt 2 shrimp with lemon spaghetti wasn’t worth the price and $16 for a chicken breast on Vodka pasta which was already $38 dollars, please. We expressed interest in the soufflé, which takes 20 minutes to make, yet once again they never came to ask for our order. So we didn’t order it and instead got the $19 tiny cheesecake. Pretty bad considering they seemed to have way too many managers just standing around doing nothing when they should’ve been making their rounds to the tables.

reviews.text: Came here for a birthday dinner. As soon as we walked in, we were immediately greeted.  Upon being seated I was wished a happy birthday and she was very pleasant on our walk to the table. .  Our server was also very nice.  I ordered the Italian Paloma, which was yummy.  My date and I shared the focaccia bread and a Caesar salad to start. The Caesar salad for a top shelf restaurant was slightly wilted and the bread was cold.  Which pretty much set the tone for the rest of our meal. I ordered the butternut squash ravioli, and my Date ordered the vodka pasta with chicken and a side of broccolini.  The food came out in a timely manner yet everything was cold. The chicken was a  $17 add on and was an overcooked, dry 4oz piece of chicken.  The broccolini was ice cold yet,  still tasty. Several tables around us were also celebrating birthdays, and I watched all of them receive a complementary piece of cake with a birthday candle in it yet I did not. I did not ask for this, but I also didn’t witness the other tables around us ask and it was stated in our reservation that it was a birthday. Overall, the front of the house restaurant staff did a good job , but the food was definitely not worth the money. Not sure we will return.

reviews.text:
I don’t normally write reviews, but this restaurant deserved every word. From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere felt warm, welcoming, and genuinely inviting. But what truly elevated the entire experience was my server, Jay. His service was hands-down some of the best I’ve ever received. Attentive without being overbearing, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about making sure every detail was perfect—he set the tone for an unforgettable meal.

As for the food… phenomenal doesn’t even come close. Every appetizer and course was crafted with such indulgence and creativity that it’s almost hard to describe. Each bite was intriguing, rich, and full of flavor in a way that kept me excited for the next dish. You can tell the kitchen takes pride in what they do, and it absolutely shows.

From start to finish, the entire staff made me feel appreciated as a guest. This place is not just a restaurant—it’s an experience worth checking out. If you’re looking for incredible service, memorable dishes, and a team that truly cares, this is the spot. I’m beyond grateful for the service and hospitality, and I can’t wait to come back.

reviews.text:
Thanksgiving Disappointment!

We had made dinner reservations for Thanksgiving, 2025 about one month at Luna by Giada.  Tonight (Nov 12th) at 7 PM I received a call from the restaurant confirming my reservation.  I was told they were having a buffet style dinner and it would be $175 per adult. First of all for $175 I expect to sit down and be served; the reason I do not want to prepare dinner myself for Thanksgiving. Also, a phone call two weeks prior to a Thanksgiving day dinner reservation is unheard of, as that is not a sufficient amount of time to find a new reservation as most restaurants are booked way in advance for a major holiday.  I suggest in the future that when booking a reservation for a holiday that Luna by Giada‘s software, or booking site has a prompt that comes up stating that their menu will not be served. It really is a shame to waste peoples time!  I was excited to eat at the restaurant having heard positive reviews, however, now I am so disappointed I may never want to eat there.
reviews.author: Anthony Aquino

reviews.text:
My husband and I made a reservation at Luna by Giada to celebrate our wedding anniversary, with expectations running high given our previous, excellent experience at Giada's Las Vegas location. Unfortunately, the experience at Luna did not meet the "fine dining" standard the price point suggests.

The service started off on a disappointing note. There was no one at the host stand to greet us upon arrival. After a short wait, the hostess asked about our outdoor seating preference and then the server asked if we were celebrating anything—both details we had specifically provided in our OpenTable reservation. This made the start feel uncoordinated. A few minutes after being seated outdoors, three staff members maneuvered a very heavy umbrella right next to our table. It was a concerning distraction and safety worry that should have been managed before the restaurant opened.

Our server, however, was a true highlight. They were very nice, attentive, had a big smile, and were eager to listen and provide helpful recommendations.

The food was generally just "okay." The focaccia was excellent, a definite high point of the meal. However, the signature spaghetti dish was surprisingly lacking in flavor. The chicken with polenta, while edible, was close to being oversalted. Desserts were better: the pumpkin soufflé was very good, but the tiramisu tasted more like a chocolate mousse.

The venue itself is beautiful, and the ambiance is lovely. However, combining the missteps in host service, the disruptive umbrella moving, and the inconsistent quality of the food, the overall experience was that of a fine dining price without the expected fine dining execution.
reviews.author: William Gonzalez Suarez

reviews.text:
We chose Luna to celebrate my fiancées birthday. We had high hopes given our past experience in Vegas and the fact that we dine out at nice restaurants often. While the atmosphere was great, the overall experience fell short.

Our server forgot our initial order of starters and drinks, which set the tone early. Once the food began arriving, it unfortunately did not match the setting. The focaccia was the highlight and really good, while the meatballs were just okay with an overpowering lemon flavor.

We held off forming a full opinion and waited for the main dishes since pasta is usually where restaurants like this really shine. When the drinks finally arrived, my old fashioned came with an ice cube so large it sat above the rim by half an inch. The server even joked about it with us and said he had told the bartender the same thing, which made it even stranger when he left it as is. The ice was not touching the liquid, it was wedged in the glass, and I had to wait about ten minutes for it to melt down enough to work as a drink.

The tortellini and nodi were both decent, but nowhere near the level you would expect at this price point.

A misstep here and there is understandable. It happens. But when several parts of the experience are off, it is worth noting. I am sharing this in hopes that someone takes a closer look and elevates things for future guests because the space and concept truly have potential.

reviews.text:
I had the opportunity to dine at Luna by Giada recently during a visit to the Caesars Republic Scottsdale. Happy hour begins at 3:30 pm and I arrived promptly at that time -- and seating is available at the bar until the dining room opens at 5 pm.

I ordered two pizzas: the Spicy Sausage and the Margherita. Both were superbly made and delicious. The Spicy Sausage wasn't all that spicy, but I like hot foods and that certainly did not detract from my enjoyment of the pizza. The proportions of sausage to cheese to peppers were ideal for the Neapolitan crust.

Also, the staff at the bar were very helpful and attentive.

There are other menu options that I want to try, so I plan to return as soon as my schedule allows. Keep up the great work!

reviews.text:
I took my wife here for our first wedding anniversary.  Being aware of this, the restaurant really went above and beyond to make our night special.  They could not have done any better.

From the start the hostess was kind and informative seating is and explaining the restaurant.  Our server was personable and very attentive.  He knew the menu and it showed.

I wasn’t sure what to expect from the food, especially with the pasta because I can be a bit of a snob.  I must say I was pleasantly surprised.  The arancini were fantastic.  The pizza, while it did not live up to the pizza I had in Naples, is probably the closest to it in the whole of phoenix.  The lemon spaghetti really is fantastic.
The pasta was good but it was a touch overcooked.  Because I had a view of the kitchen I could see that sometimes the plates were sitting at the pass for several minutes.  This is a pasta killer.  Get it out.  It will be overcooked and thicken as it sits.  Even the chicken piccata was great.

The prices seem high but actually you get a ton of food, like the corn with sausage.  It’s 14 dollars or something but they send out enough for like four people. And pasta portions are like main course portions.  That taken into consideration and I think the price is fair.

Really this is a four star review but the fact that the restaurant was staff was so amazing I have to give it a five star review

I enjoyed it so much I even got a cookbook as a souvenir.

reviews.text:
Luna by Giada is a visually stunning restaurant that reflects Giada De Laurentiis’ signature style—bright, modern, and inviting. The elegant décor and warm ambiance create a sophisticated yet comfortable dining atmosphere.

The menu features fresh ingredients with an Italian flair. The lemon spaghetti is a standout, perfectly balanced with zesty citrus and delicate pasta. The focaccia is warm and fragrant, and the small plates are ideal for sharing.

Cocktails are beautifully crafted, and the wine list is thoughtfully curated. Service was prompt and attentive, enhancing an already enjoyable dining experience.

Overall, Luna by Giada offers a refined Italian meal in the heart of Scottsdale—perfect for a special occasion or a relaxed evening out.

reviews.text: For the prices we were very underwhelmed. The appetizer focaccia bread was good and the meatballs were okay. The main courses were the dropped ball for us. The pasta was swimming in olive oil, I understand it’s a main ingredient in pesto but that’s all we could taste. Plus the noodles themselves were undercooked. Skip the pork chop, it was tender, but had no flavor otherwise. The smashed potatoes were so salty we couldn’t eat them, they went in the trash. We did not opt to try any desserts. If you want to spend $50-100 per person, save yourself and get a better experience across the street.

reviews.text: Food: Ordered the New York strip with mushrooms and I guess I missed the part where the balsamic would be drizzled all over the fine piece of meat that needed nothing else to make its flavor perfect. The cow that gave up its life for this crime against bovinity must have been churning in its grave knowing what was done with it after it sacrificed itself for this monstrosity of a dish. My wife ordered the whatever meat special with a lot of over buttered mashed potatoes. When they brought the special over, I thought it was to decide if we would want dessert after, because it was a base of over buttered mashed potatoes with a tiny piece of meat (probably 8oz) that looked like a brownie and on top a ball like scoop of more over buttered mashed potatoes (it looked like a vanilla ice cream base, with a brownie layer in the middle, and then a scoop of more vanilla ice cream on the top layer). Yes, that special was $97. Service: for a place that each person will be north of $125 ea. and 20% or more tip is expected, I expect to not have to clean the water I accidentally spilled, but I did have to clean it up myself and had to at least 3 times twist my neck like the exorcist to find someone to refill my water glass. Atmosphere: tables for 4 are tiny, dishes barely fit after I requested to have the candle and wine glasses removed. Solution: instead try Steak 44 or Le Ame across the street at The Global Ambassador.

Phenomenal! Everything we tasted was absolutely delicious and perfectly cooked. Cherise was our server and she is fantastic! She is personable, professional, and has a lovely personality. reviews.text: I had the great pleasure at eating at Giada's. I have been to Giada's restaurant in Vegas, and Luna stands at the same pinnacle. The price is very reasonable for the quality and service that is provided. The one downside I would say is parking availability close to the building itself, the parking lot is constantly full, but that only speaks to a compliment of how good the restaurant is. They do have valet parking so please be ready to bring about $12 or more for valet if you choose to go that route. Highly recommend not to skip on the bread appetizer. ✨ An Unforgettable Birthday Celebration at Luna by Giada ✨

I recently celebrated my birthday at Luna by Giada, and it was truly an unforgettable experience from start to finish. The ambiance was elegant yet welcoming, the food was exquisite (every bite was a celebration in itself), but what made the evening absolutely exceptional was our server, Jay.

Jay went above and beyond to make us feel special—his warmth, attention to detail, and genuine care added a layer of magic to the night. From expertly guiding us through the menu to surprising us with thoughtful touches throughout the evening, he made sure everything was seamless and memorable.

We laughed, toasted, and savored every moment. It wasn’t just dinner—it was an experience, and one I’ll remember for years to come. Thank you, Luna, and thank you, Jay, for making my birthday so beautifully special. We can’t wait to come back!

reviews.text:
I’ve dined at many places, but my experience at Luna ranks among the worst — not because of the food (which I never even got to try), but because of the abysmal customer service and outright incompetence of management, particularly from the so-called General Manager, Paul.

Upon arrival, we were greeted not with hospitality, but with confusion and indifference. There were clearly multiple open tables, yet we were told by the hostess staff that seating was being handled “by the computer” — a nonsensical excuse that seemed more like a way to avoid accountability than a system designed for efficiency. No logic, no flexibility, no service.

When we asked for clarification, Paul stepped in — not to help, but to escalate the situation by smugly offering us seats at the bar. That’s right: while empty tables sat untouched, the General Manager thought the best solution was to downgrade our experience and essentially dismiss our concerns. According to him, there were no pre-assigned seats, just random assignments from some mystery system. Translation: we don’t care where you sit, and we’re not going to help you.

Luna wants to present itself as a refined dining experience, but the truth is it’s run like a poorly managed chain with zero regard for the guest. If Paul is the one leading the team, it’s no wonder the front-of-house is so disorganized and indifferent.

Save yourself the frustration. Luna may have trendy decor and a curated menu, but no amount of ambiance can make up for being treated like an inconvenience. Until they learn the basics of hospitality — or hire someone who actually knows how to manage a dining room — this place deserves to be skipped, not celebrated.

The food was exceptional, and the wine selection hit every note, but what truly set the evening apart was the seamless, thoughtful service from start to finish. From the host who seated us to the server, food runner, and even the water attendant—every team member was trained to anticipate and enhance the guest experience. It was our last night in AZ and a Saturday. Seeing the reviews went ahead and made reservations.

We arrived and were sat somewhat promptly. We were greeted almost immediately with water and beverage options and about two minutes later by someone offering appetizers and bar drinks. We declined and our server arrived about 10 minutes later. She took our order and our food took a little longer than normal due to there being a lot of prom groups for the evening.

My friend ordered the meatballs which were delicious! I truly have not tasted a better meatball and my aunt by marriage is Italian so I have had authentic homemade… these were 10/10.

My daughter ordered the lemon pizza which was also really good. She enjoyed.

I ordered the filet mignon. It was excellent both by taste and tenderness.

The sides are al a cart should you choose to order one although my filet was served on a bed of potato.

The chocolate “cake” was just okay, I would not order again.

My friend and her daughter who consider themselves tiramisu connoisseurs raved about this tiramisu.

The manager was very visible and stopped by our table two times.

If in the area again, I would most definitely return.

We went for My Dads 70th birthday. The ambiance was beautiful, the food was spectacular, and the service was wonderful.

Our servers name was Shereese. She was charismatic, charming, and very attentive. Our plates and silverware were refreshed with each course. Shereese even de-crummed the wiped the table between every course. The care and attention we received is a lost art in hospitality these days, but not at Luna!!

Back to the FOOD. My Sister said it best, you never had to guess what the star of the dish was. For example you weren’t searching for bits of crab in The Crab Arancini. Generous chunks of crab as soon as you cut into it.  The calamari was perfectly battered ever so lightly with the best crunch, and a large portion at that! Plus topped with squash blossoms and sweet drop peppers!!! Chefs kiss.

And can we talk about the LEMON. There were subtle hints of lemon in almost everything we ate. If they packaged and sold their lemon butter, I would buy it!!! The food and flavors were so vibrant and refreshing, I could almost convince myself they were less calories. 😆

If you haven’t been - this place is worth the drive, the money, and the calories! Go to Luna.
reviews.author: Tricia Starwalt (Tricia Goldberg)

reviews.text:
Fun and gracious greeting from the manager and front desk. Fresh brilliantly prepared Italian cuisine with a twist. Best cocktail I’ve had all winter ( Moderna).
Arggg. The only issue was our waitress who was otherwise prompt and friendly over describing the menu with the equivalent of a primer like a Ted talk. reviews.text:
From the moment we walked into Luna by Giada, we knew we were in for something special—but our experience far exceeded expectations, thanks in large part to the exceptional service from Jay and Alonso. Jay in particular set the tone for the evening by sharing Giada’s signature philosophy: “I like to eat a little of everything, but not a lot of anything.” It was such a thoughtful touch that immediately made us feel at home and inspired our table to embrace family-style sharing.
The care and attention from the staff didn’t stop there. The manager made a point to stop by and check in, ensuring every detail of our evening was perfect—which it absolutely was.
The highlight of the meal? The evening’s special: Lemon Spaghetti with Lobster. It was the entrée of my dreams—bright, luxurious, and beautifully balanced. Every bite was pure joy.
Luna by Giada delivers not only on flavor but on hospitality, ambiance, and genuine warmth. We’ll be back—and we’ll be asking for Jay and Alonso!

reviews.text: A woman without education in a red shirt from the hotel ran me out of the parking lot because I was taking care of my dogs while my family was in the reserved room. Don't come here if you want to be treated like criminals

reviews.text: Luna is amazing! We loved our experience there! The restaurant is gorgeous and the ambiance is fabulous. We were so thankful we could sit on the patio with our dog. The hostess Bella was very friendly and helpful when I called to confirm our reservation. Kenny the manager was very welcoming. Melanie our server was so lovely. She was on top of it! Her service was impeccable and it really enhanced our experience. The seafood tower was delicious. reviews.text: This was an amazing experience. The food is sublime, especially the scallop risotto, lemon spaghetti, and the fritto misto, HIGHLY RECOMMEND ordering these. The fritto misto was a scrumptious mix of calamari and shrimp with a lemon aioli. The lemon spaghetti advocates for a diverse palette, with a tang of sourness gradually transitioning to a savory and creamy flavor. The risotto has perfectly cooked scallops with an aromatic asparagus base. The staff is very amiable and focused. Our waiter, Melanie, was very eager and thoughtful. We had a splendid time at Luna and would definitely come again!

reviews.text: The food was good (nothing especially remarkable). The service left a little to be desired. The noise was almost unbearable. The only thing over the top was the prices. We will not return.

reviews.text: Highly recommend.  The food is outstanding and the service is top notch. Friday night had an upbeat vibe and the restaurant and bar were fell. reviews.text:
I recently had the pleasure of dining at Giada‘s restaurant in Scottsdale, and I’m still thinking about the incredible experience! Jay was amazing and very attentive and friendly. Giada should be immensely proud of what she has built here in Scottsdale. This restaurant not only lives up to her reputation, but exceeds expectations in every way. I can’t wait to return and enjoy another unforgettable meal!

reviews.text: We enjoyed Giada’s Vegas restaurant so were excited to find another while visiting Scottsdale. We ordered Kir Imperials (bubbles with a splash of Chambord) but they were unable to make it (no Chambord we assumed) so had Franciacorta & it was delightful. We started by sharing the Caprese salad & it was amazing! (Who’s ever heard of Balsamic pearls?! SO good!). Oh, and do NOT forget to order the focaccia! Omg. Then we shared the Porterhouse steak with a cacio pepe raviolo plus a side of spicy Brussel sprouts & it was all really delicious. Our server, Kaitlyn, was adorable & friendly. She’s young & learning about wine so my husband, who knows quite a bit, had fun teaching her. We ordered a wonderful bottle of Pinot Noir (Patz & Hall) but the wrong glasses were brought out. He asked for something more appropriate & I guess they don’t have Burgundy glasses there but she accommodated us the best she could. After a lovely evening on the patio watching the stunning sunset, Kaitlyn brought us a Tiramisu to go with our check. So sweet & it was yummy!! We enjoyed it but the wine program needs a little work (we saw bottles on display that weren’t available on the menu, wrong glasses, no one on staff that knew anything about wine to help people navigate the list. They might benefit from an iPad wine list that can be easily updated & give patrons descriptions of the wine?!) but certainly didn’t ruin our experience.

reviews.text: I was in town visiting Scottsdale for my birthday and my sister and I went to Luna by Giada. Highly recommend this place! when I come to Scottsdale next, it will definitely be on my list.

reviews.text:
Luna by Giada is nothing short of exceptional. This was our second visit, and if anything, it only solidified our love for this gem. From the moment we walked in, we were welcomed with warmth and professionalism, setting the tone for an unforgettable evening.

The food? Absolutely stellar. Every dish was crafted with precision and packed with flavor, reflecting Giada’s signature touch of elegance and comfort. From start to finish, each bite was a masterful blend of quality ingredients and expert execution.

The service was equally outstanding. Our server was not only knowledgeable but also incredibly attentive, ensuring that every aspect of our meal was flawless. Their recommendations were spot-on, demonstrating a deep understanding of the menu. The support staff—assistants and busser—were just as impressive, working seamlessly to maintain a smooth and luxurious dining experience.

It’s rare to find a restaurant where every detail is executed with such excellence, and Luna delivers on all fronts. This certainly won’t be our last visit—we can’t wait to return!

We had an amazing Sunday brunch at Luna by Giada in Scottsdale, and it was worth every penny of the $95 per person. The meal was a top notch, featuring a lavish spread that included fresh seafood, an interactive pasta wheel, and a Tuscan carving station. The complimentary bottomless mimosas elevated the experience to pure luxury.
What truly set this brunch apart was the phenomenal service from Jay, our server. Jay’s attentiveness, warmth, and impeccable recommendations made us feel like VIPs throughout the meal. Blake, Deva, and the rest of the staff rounded out the team. It’s rare to encounter such genuinely outstanding hospitality.
The ambiance was elegant yet relaxed, creating the perfect setting for a memorable dining experience. Having dined at other exceptional restaurants in the area, we can confidently say this was among the best. Luna by Giada has set a new standard for brunch in Scottsdale—highly recommended!

For dinner we had the Lemon pasta with the Maine lobster and the chef’s special, the trio, which gave us the perfect taste of everything. We ended dinner with the tiramisu and vanilla gelato. reviews.text: A completely ok meal! They did very little to make you forget you’re eating in a hotel restaurant in terms of ambiance and prices. The bar is *right* there at the entrance and feels like somewhere between an airport bar and a Courtyard Marriott lobby bar. Had a Rose Negroni which was great though (wine list also leaves a lot to be desired). They had terrible live music — some guy who can’t sing playing covers ranging from Johnny Cash to John Mayer while simultaneously playing hits from 2005-2010’s throughout the rest of the restaurant. The focaccia was amazing. Fritto Misto was good but too much for two people. The speciality pasta, lemon spaghetti, was perfectly executed in terms of balancing lemon and mascarpone but I’m not sure I would go out of my way for it. The filet was perfectly cooked temp wise but under salted. It was served with a raviolo with a quail egg but since it was served with the pasta dish, the quail egg wasn’t runny by the time we cut into it. The presentation was beautiful. The service was great. Probably won’t be back but it was good to check it out.

reviews.text:
The glass walled open kitchen is an absolute show stopper. 🤩 We were in awe when we entered the main dining area. To be greeted by that beautiful red tile Italian stone oven—🥲 WOW. Decor was definitely on point and gives a Vegas-esque feel. 💎
Atmosphere looked lovely, however the dining area was very echoey, too much hard surface decor that left the ambient noise and chatter of the other guests bouncing off the walls. 💥🤫 This made it  difficult for my partner and I to share a conversation at our dinner table.
Wine list extensive. 🍷 Signature Luna menu items. 🍝 Interactive dessert. 🍨
Prior to our dining experience at Luna, we knew we should enjoy some seafood for dinner. 😋 🍽️ We decided on the Mediterranean Branzino and Giadas' Signature Lemon Spaghetti. 🍝 🍋 🦐 We paired this with a refreshing glass of 2021 Villa Matilde Greco Di Tufo with notes of citrus and apricot. 🍑🍋🍊 A refreshing choice to pair with food of the Italian Amalfi coast that are rich in cheese, lemon, and seafood! 🦞🍋🧀🇮🇹
My original drink choice was going to be a cocktail from the bar, 🍹 but they were out of an ingredient for it—though I was not disappointed with our choice in wine. 🍷
If you have visited the GIADA in Las Vegas located on a balcony floor of the Cromwell, you might notice a few duplicate menu items. 👯‍♀️🤩
4/5 ⭐️s 1. Dining room echoey. 🙉 2. The shrimp on the Lemon spaghetti were tough, slightly overcooked. 🔥🍤3. The Lemon spaghetti pasta sauce was very heavy. 4. Our server made a mistake on our check, it was not handled very well by management, and it took too long. 5. They were out of certain items on the menu.
Overall, a lovely experience. 🙌 We were amazed to see that this is the first non-gaming Caesars Entertainment hotel outside of Vegas. 🎰 🚫 Just a few points in dinner that were unsavory. However, I'll be back for my cocktail. 🍸
reviews.author: A. Rose

reviews.text: Luna by Giada, nestled within the Caesars Republic Scottsdale in Phoenix, offers an exceptional dining experience that masterfully blends bold Italian flavors with fresh Mediterranean influences. The ambiance is both sophisticated and welcoming, making it an ideal spot for any occasion. The Fritto Misto impresses with its perfect crunch and light, fluffy sauce, while the Sicilian Focaccia delights with its soft, pizza-like crust and generous portions. The Lemon Pizza stands out, striking a remarkable balance between citrus and savory notes, though it leans towards the oily side. For main courses, the Signature Lemon Spaghetti offers a unique twist with its slightly dry texture and subtle bitterness, complemented by perfectly cooked shrimp. The Mediterranean Branzino is a highlight, featuring tender, lemon-infused flesh and crispy skin. Cocktail enthusiasts will appreciate The Moderno, a refreshing whiskey-infused drink reminiscent of sangria, and the Isabella, a delightful take on a classic margarita. Desserts are equally impressive; the Hazelnut Soufflé is a soft, pillowy confection with just the right amount of sweetness, while the Lemon and Raspberry Gelato provides a refreshing finish, albeit without any extraordinary flair. Service is attentive, and the overall experience at Luna by Giada is one of culinary excellence and inviting atmosphere, making it a must-visit destination in Scottsdale.

reviews.text: We had the BEST experience here celebrating our anniversary! The food exceeded expectations— the signature lemon pasta was to die for!!! We also had pizza and a couple of different salads. So so so good. Kindall took such good care of us- so sweet and helpful! She really elevated the whole evening. Can’t recommend highly enough. Such a great experience!

reviews.text: Let me start by saying that we're huge fans of Giada; therefore, came in with great expectations. We went to Luna for dinner twice (two weeks apart) during February and our second visit was more disappointing than the first as far as food goes. The service was awful on our first visit with our server touching me in a very intrusive way (even poking my belly at one point) every time he stopped by to check on us. He was attentive, but in an annoying and intrusive way. Our second visit was better with a friendly, helpful, and attentive server who waited on us without being overbearing and annoying. So I guess service can be good or bad depending on where you are seated. The place is nothing to write home about, modern and well decorated, but noisy and parking at the venue can be difficult. We parked at the Mall parking lot and walked across. Oh and be prepared to pay for a Venue Fee of 3.5% of your bill. I can't tell you why or what for, but it is added to your bill. There was music playing during our second visit which was loud and distracting (perhaps this is the justification for the venue fee). No thank you! Now the food... Our first visit was to try the pasta. Her being Italian and with all the shows we watched her cook, we thought we were going to be in for a treat. The pictures on the website look great, but don't be fooled by good marketing. We ordered the Focaccia (very delicious and perhaps the best item on the menu), Caprese Salad (very ordinary), Crab Arancini (flavorless and someone should have invited the crab to join the party), Lemon Spaghetti (good, but not great), Tripolini Pasta (sour sauce and just a faint flavor of short rib), and Citrus Ricotta Cheesecake for dessert (soggy and spongy flavorless mess, but pretty to look at). We were told that the citrus ricotta cheesecake was made with a shot of limoncello in it, but they either ran out or forgot to mix it in because there was no citrus flavor in the cheesecake at all. Our second visit was to try the pizza. After all anyone can have a bad day in the kitchen and perhaps our persistence would be rewarded with great pizza to rave about to friends and family. Well... sometimes persistence slaps you in the face like you stole something... Our second visit was more disappointing and frustrating than the first. We ordered an Arugula Salad which promised crispy pancetta and candied lemons, but the lemons did not join, the pancetta was very cold and very hard, and the arugula looked wilted and tasted as if it had been plated and refrigerated from the day before. Then we ordered the Bacon Dates (chewy bacon with an awful tasting red sauce). The portion is 5 to a serving and we only ate 2, but the nail in our coffin was the pizza. We ordered a Margherita Pizza (my favorite) and a Lemon Pizza (novelty and never had it before, so why not?). Well... the Margherita pizza was burnt (the dough was bitter and charred, the sauce was very sour, and the mozzarella was scarce - like eating a burnt and sour piece of soggy cardboard). The lemon pizza wasn't as appalling, but it was flavorless with a taste of sour milk when one bit the part that had the lemon mixed with the cheese. This pizza needed some salt and and additional ingredient to liven the flavor, or at least to give it flavor and not just a warm, greasy, sour milk flavor on pizza dough. It is pretty sad when one can get better pizza from one's local high end grocer, than from a high end restaurant from a celebrity chef. In closing, the food is way overpriced for the quality. The pasta should have been the best pasta we ever had for the price, but one dish was good, and the other was mediocre at best, and the pizza was the most offensive assault on the human palate ever contrived. That being said, we wouldn't return to Luna if Giada herself extended an invitation. We can't in good conscience recommend this place to anyone.

We went here for date night and we usually go to fine/classy restaurants and this place is  beautiful. We’re food network fans and try to visit the celebrity chef restaurants so we were excited to try Luna.
Good attentive service without being annoying; but like others have mentioned, everything is somewhat overpriced for what you get. I feel the focaccia bread starter should just be provided, certainly not worth the charging price. The Caprese salad was fantastic and the balsamic pearls were incredible.. kinda like caviar almost.
Cocktails were OK, but not very strong and also a bit higher than typical even for Scottsdale.
The Lemon spaghetti was unique and comes with 2 shrimps.. I added 2 more at $10 each. It was delicious and enjoyable. The lemon pizza was good too. The most memorable, unique dish was dessert soufflé. I can’t recall any other restaurant that offers this, so it was definitely worth trying and very light and delicious.
This is a great place for a date or to impress clients. Everything is a premium probably just because it’s at Caesars, so be prepared when the check arrives.

reviews.text:
I've given two stars for service because our server was well meaning, but the booth was awkward & uncomfortable, the prices were outrageous ($15 for an order of focaccia that's not even made in-house, pastas hovering around $40, vegetable side dishes for $17) and the atmosphere was unnervingly loud.

We checked in for our party of 6 and were seated at a booth.  Every place setting had a menu on it, yet we were asked by a server if anyone else would be joining us.  Strange.  The reservation time passed and we thought it was odd that no one in the party had arrived.  Sure enough, the hostess seated them after us at a booth across the room and fortunately one of the couples saw us 5 minutes later.

Italian food can be easily "veganized" so we never worry when dining out.  Not only is there not a single vegan item on the menu, but the only two vegetables available to us were broccolini and potatoes.  Apparently, every other vegetable in the kitchen is either prepared in pancetta fat or butter.  I explicitly said I did not want to order multiple $17 sides of vegetables but that I simply wanted a plate with a little assortment of whatever vegetables the kitchen could prepare.  Our server completely understood what I was going for.  But then what comes out to me?  A side order of olive oil soaked broccolini and a bowl of crispy potatoes.  Basically, the equivalent of a middle finger from the kitchen.

My husband opted to try spaghetti with the suggested substitution of a pomodoro sauce (instead of all of the cream and cheese based sauces on the menu).  He said it tasted like a can of tomato paste was dumped on top and there was no seasoning.

Even if you're on an expense account, I would not recommend Luna by Giada.  There are too many excellent, correctly priced, restaurants in Scottsdale where your time, money and calories would be better spent.

If you’re looking for an unforgettable dining experience, Luna by Giada should be at the top of your list.

She had an impeccable knowledge of the menu and offered excellent recommendations. Every dish was explained with such enthusiasm, and her suggestions were spot on. reviews.text:
Good not Great - We are local and visit many restaurants in the area. We were excited to experience Giada's food after watching her on TV. I think the expectation was to experience something great, but the food and ambience just fell flat.

- Food: The drinks were nice, but the food just wasn't anything special. We had a couple apps, a pasta course (famous lemon spaghetti), and a main course (Bronzino). It's odd with the kitchen being wide open (big windows) and you see the famous lemon spaghetti has the sauce just poured out of a pitcher onto the noodles. There are so many great restaurants in the area with better quality.

- Servers: Our servers were nice, but you could tell they were not accustom to a nicer dinning experience. We kept on getting asked questions at awkward times. Didn't clean plates when they were empty and asked when they were half full if we were finished. It just didn't feel orchestrated well. Manager even stood by our table and smiled at us, but never attempted to make an introduction.

- Ambience: It is a beautiful location. The feel is very upscaled. I actually like the open kitchen. The only thing funny was the large red pepper grinder. It just feels gimmicky.

- Price: I think this was the biggest shocker. Honestly for the price I would think I am in a very fine dining restaurant. If it was more aligned to the quality, I probably wouldn't have done this review.
---- Example: We like to start the evening with one tequila shot, usually Don Julio 1942. Many well known high-end restaurant in the area are $40 to $50. Yes, it's silly, but we are out for a fun night. Luna wanted $80. We didn't order them. The food seemed to have a similar disparity in the price.

I doubt we will ever come back unless someone else is paying. I wouldn't even consider this place if it was a special birthday or anniversary night.

reviews.text: I thought we would have had a completely different experience after reading the reviews for this restaurant. The evening did not start out well. We were a party of six and they gave us a table in the back with two chairs and a booth style arrangement. Two of us were literally sitting on the edge of the booth. When we asked if our table could be changed to something more comfortable, we were told the other tables were reserved for the evening, even though I counted at least 10 tables that were available. I did not understand why our table could not be switched with a reservation that had not been checked in yet. The cocktail list was unimpressive. The cocktails are generously priced, however did not have the flavors as advertise and had very little alcohol in them. The pasta was undercooked and to the point of being hard. Unfortunately was not edible. We order a side that never was served but ended up being charged for it. At the end of the night when we went to get the car from valet, they simply handed the keys to us and pointed in the direction of the car, which was parked a distance away. The attendant had no intention of bringing the car up to the front, which is what you would expect when you were paying for valet service. Overall, a very disappointing night for a four figure price tag. Definitely will not be returning to this restaurant. I am so confused by the positive reviews that I have read as it just did not match our experience. There are so many great restaurants in the area at this price point and this one is simply not worth it.

reviews.text:
I had been wanting to try this restaurant for a long time. I highly recommend making a reservation, as seating is limited. The space has an open-concept design, allowing you to see directly into the kitchen.

While the service was generally good, our bottle of wine was forgotten, and the pacing of our courses felt off.

The drinks were quite expensive, with cocktails ranging from $22 to $25. Surprisingly, some were made with basic Stoli vodka, which felt underwhelming for the price.

We sampled a variety of dishes, starting with the bacon-wrapped dates and the crab arancini. The arancini was outstanding—perfectly fried, with incredibly fresh crab, served alongside a flavorful spicy red sauce.

For entrees, we ordered the lemon spaghetti, spicy sausage pizza, scallop risotto, and nodi marini alla vodka. Unfortunately, the pizza was a letdown—undercooked in the center and lacking flavor. However, the scallop risotto and lemon spaghetti were exceptional. Both dishes featured high-quality seafood and stood out for their unique flavors.

The highlight of the meal, without question, was the tiramisu. It was one of the best I’ve ever had.

Overall, the experience was good, but I wouldn’t return due to the steep prices and the food not quite living up to them.

Ordered the scallop risotto which was great just lacking in service.

Granted it was New Year’s Eve, our server was in the room maybe every 20-30 minutes and was quickly out to be with her other tables.

Would recommend for lunch or happy hour but not on peak nights/weekends/holidays. Won’t be back for a long time.

reviews.text: The uncomfortable truth is that I find many of these reviews overly welcoming and the use of flowery language looks concocted. My experience was lack luster but I haven’t lost all hope. Atmosphere was nice. Soft lighting  with a modern look will greet you. We were seated in what I can only describe as a booth / table combination. The table was not custom designed for this type of seating which left little room for the two people on the ends of the table leaving them wedged in their seats and very uncomfortable. It’s odd that so much attention and money went to the aesthetics of this place and yet they wouldn’t spend money for customized tables to fit so that guests would enjoy their meal. Our server was welcoming and friendly. Her wine suggestions were overly pushy on the commercially available mediocre Costco-ish wines. Her two meal suggestions were coincidentally the two highest prices entrees. So, I opted to grab the attention of the person filling our water and asked her for her recommendations. Her recommendations were spot on. Stick to the top few pasta dishes and she highly recommended the Chicken piccata.  The food was wonderful, but certainly they traded off flavor for presentation on the chicken dish.  Giada’s signature lemon pasta was super flavorful but horribly dry.  So, some room for improvement. The focaccia was wonderful and we also ordered the pizza as an appetizer which did not disappoint. Getting our table cleared and checking out felt like walking the Bataan-Corregidor Death March. Painfully slow. I tipped well as it looked like our server may have been the only one managing too many tables (not her fault) and her recommendations were clearly coached for profiteering. I would recommend this place with the caution that it has a money grab aspect to it, but some menu items redeem all the bad and worth a second visit.

Dining at Luna by Giada was truly an unforgettable experience! From the moment we stepped inside, we were enveloped in an inviting atmosphere that perfectly blends elegance with a warm, welcoming vibe. The décor is stunning, with soft lighting and beautiful Italian-inspired accents that set the stage for a memorable evening.

Our waitress, Shereese, was the epitome of exceptional service. Her knowledge of the menu was impressive, and she guided us through the delectable offerings with enthusiasm and genuine passion for the food. Shereese made us feel like valued guests, taking the time to understand our preferences and recommending dishes that exceeded all expectations.

Every dish we ordered was a masterpiece! The flavors were vibrant and authentic, showcasing Giada’s signature Italian cuisine. From the perfectly cooked pasta to the luscious desserts, each bite was a celebration of culinary excellence. The attention to detail in presentation was equally remarkable, making our meal not just delicious but visually stunning as well.

To top it all off, Shereese continued to check in on us throughout the evening, ensuring our glasses were always full and our dining experience was nothing short of perfect. Her warm personality added an extra layer of joy to our evening, making it feel like we were dining with a friend rather than just a waitress.

Luna by Giada is a gem that I can’t recommend highly enough! With fantastic food and outstanding service from Shereese, this restaurant offers a dining experience that is truly special. I can't wait to return and explore more of the menu—I have a feeling it will be even better the second time around!

reviews.text: Perfect 77F evening! Sat outdoor and the atmosphere was great. Perfect weather, nice music that was perfect volume allowing for comfortable conversation. The gentle trickle of the fountain in the background. Just great.  Service! Sherese was awesome! She was kind, engaging, attentive…..couldn’t ask for a better server.   I should keep her name a secret because we will be requesting her in the future and we don’t want her to be too busy for us.  The food was great.  Giada obviously loves her lemon and there is a hint of lemon to many of the dishes.  Lemon Cesar…10/10 but too big for one person…..I would suggest you share. Mushroom pizza, focaccia bread to die for. Branzino crispy and perfectly prepared and presented. Dessert…….hazelnut soufflé was great and light but the lemon cookies were to die for.  Great food, great service, perfect night for outdoor dining with great outdoor tables. What more can you ask for???
reviews.author: Gordon Cohen

reviews.text:
5 stars isn’t enough to rate the Luna experience the hostesses, bar tenders, servers, cooks and chefs created for me. From the moment I walked in, I knew I was in for an unforgettable experience. I didn’t know how right I would be.

We were off to a great start when the Sicilian Focaccia, Arugula Salad and Shellfish Tower arrived with all their assorted butters and sauces. The bits of crispy pancetta in the salad were a particular highlight!

My Nodi Marino ala Vodka was the perfect entree to follow up those apps and the Citrus Ricotta Cheesecake for dessert made this a meal I won’t soon forget!

The food was only outdone by the staff who helped us navigate the menu. Shereese’s background of the restaurant on the way to our table, knowledge of the food and wine menus, making the perfect recommendations based on what we said we were looking for, and her focus on us as if we were the only ones in the restaurant even though there must have been a thousand things going on, on a busy Saturday night, made this a one of a kind evening.

Brody’s easy going and welcoming nature and willingness to chat about things other than food for a bit, gave us that “we’re eating with friends and family” feeling that made us feel like we weren’t just customers, and that just doesn’t happen enough.

Thanks Shereese, Brody, Giada and everyone else whose names I don’t know for a memorable and delicious night that everyone else won’t know they are trying to live up to.
reviews.author: David Lopata

reviews.text: My friend and I went to dinner for his birthday. We had the best experience . The food was absolutely fantastic . We told our server Shereese to just choose her favorite options , and we weren’t disappointed. Started our experience with some amazing wine and delicious cocktails. We had the focaccia bread which was by far the most delicious bread I’ve ever had , we also had the seafood tower which was so fresh and delicious . We had several other appetizers and our entree was the branzino fish , it was so delicious the skin was crispy and the fish moist and flaky it was AMAZING , we also had an amazing pasta which had the most delicious sauce and Italian sausage. We ended our meal with the most amazing cheesecake with lemon it was airy and creamy absolutely the best I’ve ever had , oh and the lemon ricotta cookies were to die for . Thank you so much to Chef Austin McNeely and Chef Johnny Austin for making such amazing food . The freshness was impeccable. Also Sheresse our server knew every ingredient and explained everything as she brought it out and she was so friendly and kind and loving . We will for sure request her the next time we visit  . I would highly recommend visiting Luna . I am already planning my next dinner with my daughters who love Giada and are so excited to try the delicious food .
