reviews.text:
I'm really torn about this review. Based on what we were hearing and the general info we had pretty high expectations. That's probably unfortunate but given that we spent $700 for 3 people, the high bar seems appropriate.
First off the food was fine, It wasn't great but prepared well. Biggest complaint here was that everything had something else in it (fennel covered filet) etc.. The real issue was the atmosphere. Started off with a hostess that gave us the immediate confusion about how classy the establishment may or may not be. We were served the wrong drinks, which isn't a problem except that the resulting conversation was just filled with awkwardness. We had no less than 6 different people at our table, asking if we were done with something or bringing us (the wrong) water.. There were 4 tables in our area of the dining room and the constant stream of waiters/bussers was simply distracting. Our main waitress was good. Perhaps a tad too friendly, but charming.  Overall everything was just missing the level of professionalism that you expect at finer establishments. "Did you want more tap water?", "Were these [wine glasses] in the way or are you using them?",  "Are you guys going to finish that or do you want a doggie bag?" (on our bread appetizer that clearly wasn't finished yet.), Weird things said from bussers and those running water.  Bussers also reaching across the table in unnatural ways. The food runners were fine for what it's worth. (Except that first guy, but he clearly hasn't worked food service before).
Overall it really felt like we paid 1st string  prices for the 3rd string team. It was not what we were hoping to experience. Also,  there were three babies in the dining room. I love babies as much as the next person, but the guy directly in front of me is feeding an infant with a bottle, the table next to us was fumbling with their stroller the whole time and another toddler crying from an unknown location.  It was just an overall run of the mill experience. Maybe we should have gone on Friday or Saturday. Unfortunately we'll never know.

reviews.text:
If we have been Yelp friends for while, you would know that one of the things I hate the most in this world is for my arch-nemesis, Jon H., to be right. On top of that, he has been going off, non-stop about how disappointed he was over my man, Bobby Flay's, restaurant. So when I tell ya I came into Luna by Giada, Giada De Laurentiis being Jon's honey-babe, just waiting to hate on this place, you best believe it. I will now sit here and say that I'm not even a fan; I'm an air conditioner!

The four of us ordered two beers (Huss Blonde Ale and The Shop Crispy --- Yay to Arizona drafts), a bottle of Duckhorn wine, the Arugula Salad, The Citrus Caesar Salad, all four pizza offerings, Limoncello Souffle, and the Mascarpone Brownie Cheesecake.

Arugula Salad (Crispy Pancetta, Candied Lemons & Parmigiano Reggiano): This has pancetta. What else do you need? You can't go wrong with a peppery arugula salad.

Citrus Caesar Salad (Citrus Caesar Dressing, Parmigiano Reggiano, Focaccia Croutons & Crispy Capers): Had I been wearing a skirt, this salad would have made it flip. This is the salad that I would order for myself and eat it with a side of fries. Flavorful, cheesy, and oh so good. That subtle brightness of the citrus is oh so pleasing.

Signature Margherita (Roasted Campari Tomatoes, Basil & Mozzarella): I judge a pizza place by their margherita. It's a simple and classic combination and if you can do this right, you know the rest will be amazing. This was perfection. The sauce had a pleasant sweetness that you just can't compare.

Lemon Pizza (Mozzarella, Garlic Creme Sauce & Caciocavallo Cheese): My favorite of the four pizzas easily. I love a good pucker and this pizza is all about balance. Cheese on cheese on cheese, garlic, cream, lemon... these are all my favorite things on a perfectly charred crust. My mouth has turned into a waterfall just typing this out.

Mortadella Bianca (Parmigiano Reggiano, Shaved Mortadella & Pistachio): We learned that they will be taking this off the menu soon for a mushroom pizza. Sad. Jon H. was going on and on about how he had a hankering for some Oscar Mayer bologna after eating this. ;D I kid. If I were to be honest, out of the four pizzas, this one shined the dullest. I was expecting it to be the winner as another pizzeria in town does a similar pizza with pistachio, parmesan, and red onions and it's one of my favorites. The Mortadella Bianca wasn't bad. Girl was just got lost in a star-studded pizza family.

Spicy Sausage (Roasted Peppers, Scamorza & Oregano): Now that's a spicy meatball! (Jon H.: No one Italian really says that, Joyce!) It's not really spicy for a walking chili pepper like me but I like a bite. If something bites me, Imma bite back! This was my second favorite slice of the night.

Limoncello Souffle (Blueberry Anglaise & Candied Lemon Biscotti): Get your camera out and be prepared to record. What my girl Giada and I lack in height (short girls unite), this souffle makes up for. Is this a skyscraper!? The taller the souffle, the closer to God. Great flavors and good balance. A dessert that's light and not too sweet? It's my kinda dessert.

Mascarpone Brownie Cheesecake (Vanilla Bean Cheesecake, Brownie, Espresso Caramel & Mascarpone Whipped Cream): We were told this cheesecake gets sold out nearly every night and I can see why. As a big cheesecake fan, this hit all the right notes. Speaking of notes...

Every time a gentleman in a sharp suit walked by, the sensual notes of a saxophone permeated the air. I later found out that Kenny G is their manager. KENNY G! Don't believe me? Ask the staff! Tell them Jon H. said so! ;D

The food was spectacular and the staff was amazing. A big shout out to Jay and Damian for the amazing service.

reviews.text:
Luna by Giada offers a dining experience that is nothing short of extraordinary. From the moment we arrived, we were treated to impeccable service by Shereese, whose attentiveness and deep knowledge of the menu made our evening truly special. Her table-side manner was not only professional but also warm and engaging, adding a personal touch that enhanced our entire experience.

The food, crafted by the talented Chef Austin, and the rest of the kitchen staff was simply divine. Every dish was a masterpiece, bursting with flavor and beautifully presented. Chef Austin's gracious presence and attention to detail were evident in every bite, making the meal unforgettable.

A special thanks also goes to Brody, whose contributions added to the overall excellence of the evening. The team at Luna by Giada created an atmosphere of warmth and luxury that made our night one to remember. If you're looking for an unforgettable dining experience, Luna by Giada is the place to be.

reviews.text: I took my brother here for his 70th Birthday. The manager came to our table and welcomed us, that was a very nice touch. The staff was amazing and paid so much attention to detail!  Our server Melanie, is one of the best waitress's I have had anywhere.  She could easily work at Dominick’s or the Monarch. I think many of the staff member could. Managements must treat them right for them to be so professional. The food was good. My brother said the bread was the best he ever had.  The oysters were small but fresh and tasty. The salads where unique and fresh and quite good, but do not closely resemble Caesar or Caprese. I think the one called Caprese, my brother had, may have been better than a traditional caprese salad. My salad was not a Caesar salad, they should call it something else IMHO, but it was exactly as Melanie described to me, so I was not surprised nor disappointed when I got it.  Light Lemon dressing was refreshing for the summer.  For my cocktail I had the “LA STRADA” Stoli Cucumber Vodka, Belle de Brillet, Re’al Kiwi puree, Lemon Juice & Club Soda. My brother has 2 Mocktails of it.  It was delicious and refreshing. Perfect for summer.  When it came time for dessert, I explained to Melody I wanted a desert as well, and my brother does not share his food (not kidding) so she brought me a birthday dessert as well. Wow! I never expected that! LOL! Melanie ROCKS!!! The entire staff does. We sat in the Jade room because we a bit older and needed a quiet place to hear each other’s conversation. By the time the restaurant was full, we could no longer hear each other at all unfortunately.   But it was very good, I had the Lemon Spaghetti with scallops instead of Shrimp. The scallops were a bit underdone, a bit translucent in the middle, but I did not mention it. I’ll fix it when I make the left overs. My brother’s rare ribeye was excellent he said, and he raved about the corn and sausage side dish. The gelato and cookie dessert were heaven!  Thank you, Melanie and staff, at Luna for making my brothers 70th birthday so great.

reviews.text: What started off a little shaky turned out to be such a wonderful experience here at Luna by Giada. I’d made a reservation and 2 days prior attempted to add a 7th person. I just couldn’t get a call back to save my life. But in the end I messaged through OpenTable and got a response quite quickly. So, thats my suggestion if anyone is ever having an issue with reservations. Aside from that, once we were seated the fun began! It was my birthday and the manager was extra helpful with service and even brought us a round of the most delicious Limoncello- WOW!! Our server was a super spunky gentleman with equally impressive glasses. Thank you, Sir, for your sense of humor and wit to match our own. We also tried just about everything on the menu but my favorite would have to be the Lemon Pasta. The Mediterranean Branzino was a close second. It’s so hard to say I didn’t also love the Lemon pizza which made it home in a to-go box too. Couldn’t leave that guy behind. Some equally delicious appetizers we tried were the Fritto Misto, Sicilian Focaccia and Crab Arancini which id definitely order again. The Agnolotti pillows of heaven filled with veal were mouth watering. The Nodi Marini Alla Vodka and Chicken Panzanella plates were also devoured. Scrumptious sides that I would say you must try even if you don’t typically like goat cheese was the Goat Cheese and Balsamic Asparagus. The lemon crispy potatoes - ugh still drooling for these salty, crispy little devils. Dessert we ordered and the ladies loved were the Mascarpone Brownie Cheesecake & Chocolate Amoretti cake. I opted for a cup of their very smooth and aromatic coffee before we hit Seven (the lounge) upstairs. It was the perfect ending to the night with the pool deck and couches where we watched the storm and played Catch Up. I’d say this gang will most definitely be back.

reviews.text: I expected a great meal and was not disappointed.  It's a nicely appointed space, open but not too loud.  I love the open kitchen, but it was behind floor to ceiling glass so you did not have to hear it.  We ordered "family style" by selecting multiple dishes to share,  For Starters, we got a Caesar Salad, Bacon Wrapped Dates and the Mortadella Bianca Pizza.  The salad was large, light and lemon forward, kind of what you would expect from Giada.  The dates were stuffed with sausage and bacon wrapped, just a great combination of flavor and texture.  The mortadella pizza was very interesting.  Take a look at the picture.  Tasted great.  For Pastas we had the Agnolotti, the Modi Marini Alla Vodka and the Mezzi Rigatoni.  The Agnolotti was just average.  Almost no real flavor.  The Modi was quite good, would have liked a little more heat (spice), but the Rigatoni was spectacular.  The pasta cooked just perfect and the mushroom sauce with it was rich with ummami, deep and earthy.  It was the star of the table according to all.  For Entrees we had the Pork chap Saltimbocca and the Branzino.  The fish was delicious with a great light sauce and very crispy skin on the filters.  The pork chop was also quite good.  We finished the meal with the lemoncello souffle and the Brownie Cheesecake along with Galleano, Lemoncello and sambucca.  Let's talk service for a moment.  The food runners were super, bringing the food with a description of each dish without interrupting.  The kitchen moved things out quickly but we were not rushed.  But the highlight was our server, Shereese.  Shereese knew the menu intimately, gave great incite, was so very attentive, understood we wanted to share and enjoy slowly and she kept a great rhythm at the table.  She is a star.  Fun, engaging and highly professional.  WE had a great time!

The food is nothing short of wonderful, and prepared to perfection! The service is unmatched, Brandi is amazing and a true asset to the staff! reviews.text:
The curb appeal at Luna’s is high, as you pull up to Caesar’s, which is an amazing hotel and destination in itself.

Coming to the front reservation table, the view of the restaurant is gorgeous, with an open view of the bar and a huge wall of wines just behind.

The restaurant is gorgeous! So well designed and decorated! We all just looked at each other excited for the evening!

The menu and cocktails were grand! Everything was so good — the Riso Amaro cocktail, the Siccilian Focaccia to start, and the Mushroom Rigatoni - WOW!

Our server was super personable, and had great recommendations and anecdotes alone the way!

The only thing I would really ding Luna hard for is their acoustics — it’s SO loud in here, and it shouldn’t be! Multiple times through the night my party and I had to sit awkwardly while nearby tables roared with laughter, drowning us out completely. At any point, we could sit and tell you exactly what nearby tables were saying, as if we were sitting at their table with them. It’s really bad! I truly hope they address this with some sound baffling as right now I would have a hard time coming back with others. It’s just too hard to talk with your friends!

reviews.text:
Truly a 5-Star Dining Experience!

For a starter, the BUGATTI FOCCIA bread board is a must; I think anyone will tell you that! The focaccia bread is served with a lemon-marscapone butter, fresh pesto, and a balsamic & olive oil mix--it was an extraordinary start. Our server, Shereese, suggested spreading a touch of the creamy butter on the bread before dipping it into one of the other dishes, and that truly elevated the experience. I can see why Giada's olive oil and balsamic vinegar are famous, because the pesto and the "balsamic & oil" dips were both on a whole different level. I'm planning to return with my friends and make a meal of that and the Caprese Salad!

The CAPRESE SALAD was phenomenal--an absolute must-try. Instead of mere mozzarella, it featured creamy stracciatella cheese, and the bite-sized wedges of multicolored tomatoes were incredibly fresh. An amazing balsamic and pesto drizzle surrounded it, with balsamic molecular gastronomy pearls literally bursting with incredible flavor.

For my entrée, I had Giada's SIGNATURE LEMON SPAGHETTI, which was perfectly twisted in a creamy mascarpone cheese lemon sauce, with crispy capers (which I absolutely loved), and two shrimp. As Shereese placed it before me, she said, "Chef Giada recommends tipping the pasta over into the sauce." My little tip is to have some freshly ground pepper added (from their cool 3-foot-high pepper grinders). My husband had the SCALLOP RISOTTO. The risotto was perfectly cooked and delicious, with peas, asparagus, Maryland crab, and topped with two scallops. Both dishes were generously sized and filling.

They offered several unique cocktails, many made with gin. I opted for "The Moderno," which included Smoke Wagon small batch bourbon, Giffard orgeat syrup, lemon juice, Bigallet China China liqueur, with a splash of Super Tuscan wine floating on top. Personally, I would have preferred more fruit-forward options that weren't as strong, so given the cocktail price of $21, I will order a soft drink next time. However, if you enjoy creative, well-crafted, strong cocktails made with premium spirits, you will find excellent options here.

Our server, Shereese, made the dinner so special & memorable. Not only is she impeccably professional with honest recommendations and a deep knowledge of every detail of the menu, but she also possesses a genuinely poised and clever personality. She checked on us so many times and always at the perfect moments (even though the restaurant was packed). Her phrasing was so refined yet full of refreshing personality, like when she said, "I feel like I'm stealing your plate, but it looks as if you are finished," instead of asking, "Are you finished?" or when she said, "I won't hold you hostage; I'll get you the check," always in such a clever but respectful manner. She just exuded joy & positivity.

For dessert, Shereese brought us their famous round cheesecake-on-brownie, beautifully decorated and garnished. It was so incredible that we ate as much as we could at the restaurant and the rest at home.

Paul, the general manager, was incredibly personable and came over to wish us a happy anniversary after we received the check. He ensured that we enjoyed everything and that the dessert was comped, which Shereese had already taken care of.

They obviously informed the valet when we were ready to leave, because our car was waiting at the door, and one of the (all very special) valets said, "We appreciate you, Sir."

Everything (and everyone) was exceptional, but requesting Shereese as your server is a must.

We will definitely return!

reviews.text: Our experience going to Luna was a good one. We arrived and our table was ready. We opted to dine outside and when we stepped to the terrace, there was only a couple in another table. Inside was full and noisy so I was glad to be away from everyone. The service was excellent although the waiter mixed our drinks up but no matter. I ordered The Moderno which is a mixture of bourbon and wine (Super Tuscan) it was sublime and recommend if you like a bittersweet taste. I ordered the lemon pizza because I was curious and it did not disappoint. Very sophisticated taste. Overall a good experience but my only negative is once the couple left, we were all alone outside and felt a bit ostracized. I recommend offering a table inside if we are the only outside or when making reservations don’t offer the patio if there is only one table that will be occupied

We were embarrassed we bought another couple to such a disaster.  $500+ later... we sat at bar first & had to ask for a cocktail list 3 times & finally asked someone beside us for theirs since the bartender was "too busy" for us (It was not that full).  When we were asked to be seated we requested our bottle of wine & 2 poured glasses to come to the table.  After 20 minutes the wine bottle arrived, minus our 2 full glasses???  Anyhow ordered another bottle (not cool).  We ordered the $152 steak & the server asked quickly do we want the sauce on it?  What sauce is it (had no idea).  He right away said "I don't now what it is" ?!??! and literally ran away!  (It was a cream sauce that we did try = was "ok" BUT why did the server not know what he was serving ????). The steak was VERY UNDERWHELMING and no taste and certainly NOT worth $152!  The signature pasta dish came barely warm & when we pointed out the cool pasta it came back microwaved 30 seconds later NOT re-fired.  The side lemon potatoes were terrible & dry and we didn't eat.  The decor and atmosphere is cold & not inviting or any "Italian feel" to it.  (1 area looks like a doctors office door entrance - sterile).
